newsitem.title: FRANCE: FIGURE SKATING-SLUTSKAYA COMPLETES RUSSIAN TITLE SWEEP.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-SLUTSKAYA COMPLETES RUSSIAN TITLE SWEEP.

text.p: Irina Slutskaya gave Russia an unprecedented clean sweep of the titles by retaining the women's crown at the European figure skating championships on Saturday.
The fresh-faced Moscow teenager survived a couple of shaky landings but proved to be in a class of her own as she underlined that she is far and away the best in Europe.

After her opponents all faltered in pursuit in a disappointing session of skating, the 17-year-old physical education student, skating last, completed six triple jumps to win the free programme comfortably, just as she did in Friday's short programme.
Eight of the nine judges rated her first in the free skating and she finished with the best possible score of 1.5 factored placements.
"I could have done better. It is important for me now that I go home and work on all my elements for the world championships in March, not just one or two of them," she said.
She landed her opening triple lutz off balance and lost balance on a double loop but stayed up and finished strongly.
It was the first ever sweep at the European championships, though the old Soviet Union or Russia had won three titles on seven previous occasions.
But they had never taken the women's crown before Slutskaya claimed it last year.
"I thought about it, it is true, but in real life it doesn't touch me very much," she said.
Alexei Urmanov in the men's, Marina Eltsova and Andrei Bushkov in the pairs and Oksana Gritschuk and Evgeny Platov in the dance won the earlier titles.
Krisztina Czako of Hungary, 18, had trouble with her jumps but with those behind her also failing to live up to expectations she held on to second place with 5.0 placements.
She scaled a triple lutz down to a double and stumbled on two other landings but did not fall.

Yulia Lavrenchuk of Ukraine, also 18, fell once but did enough to move up two places to third as Vanessa Gusmeroli of France, third before the free skating, dropped to sixth behind Elena Liashenko of Ukraine.
Russian Maria Butyrskaya, a gold medal prospect before the competition, salvaged something from the wreckage of her short programme by climbing five places to fourth.
Leggy Czech Lenka Kulovana, fourth overnight, fell away to 11th place.
German 14-year-old Eva-Maria Fitze stamped herself as a star of the future by completing eight triple jumps, though not all of them cleanly, as she advanced five places to seventh.

Former silver medallist Olga Markova took eighth place ahead of five-times champion Surya Bonaly of France, who fell twice in an erratic programme which pointed up her lack of practice since recovering from Achilles tendon surgery last year.
